sentences.text:
The present claim petition was filed U/s 166 read with Section 140 of The Motor Vehicle's Act,
1988, by the petitioners.
My Ld Predecessor after conducting the inquiry passed award dated 16.05.2014.

The award was challenged before the Hon'ble High Court by the Insurance Company vide MAC Appeal No. 583/2014 .The Hon'ble High Court after hearing arguments of the appellant (Insurance Company ) as well as respondents No.1 to 3 ( Claimants), vide its order dated 12.05.2016,
has passed the following orders:

" The insurer which has been fastened with the liability has come in the appeal stating that the evidence of PW3 about the employment of deceased and his earnings therefrom has been wrongly believed without any corroborative proof, particularly as the witness took a plea that the records maintained by her office respecting all the employees has been destroyed in a fire incident.

During the course of argument when question arose as to why the oral word of PW3 with regard to the employment and earnings of the deceased should be believed, the counsel for the claimants submitted that he is agreeable to the appeal of the insurance company being allowed and the impugned judgment to the extent it awarded compensation to be set aside but requests that he be given further opportunity to adduce proper evidence to corroborate the case about the employment and earnings as cogent evidence in this regard is available.
Having regard to the above facts and circumstances, the prayer of both sides is accepted.
The impugned judgment to the extent it calculated and awarded compensation is set aside.
The matter MACT No.1011/2018 Old No. 275/2012 Praveen Bains Vs Munna Rai & ors Page No. 2 of 5 to the limited extent of calculating the compensation is remitted to the tribunal for further inquiry.

entities.text: MACT No.1011/2018 Old No. 275/2012 Praveen Bains Vs Munna Rai & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During such further inquiry, the claimants shall be allowed opportunity to lead further evidence.
Needless to add, the parties which contest shall be entitled to cross examine the witnesses additionally examined by the claimants and also lead evidence in rebuttal, if any.

The parties shall appear before the tribunal for such purposes on 19.07.2016"
2.

So the Hon'ble High Court has set aside the impugned award only to the extent of loss of dependency since the Ld Predecessor of this Court has relied upon the oral statement of PW3 qua the employment of deceased Rakesh S/O Sanjhi Ram in M/s Lazeez Affairs, without any corroboration.
And accordingly by the consent of petitioners and insurance company the compensation qua the loss of dependency was set aside.

The Hon'ble High Court has also given an opportunity to respondent No.1 to 3 ( herein petitioners in the present claim) to adduce evidence and also given an opportunity ( herein respondent No.3) to adduce evidence in rebuttal.
3. After receiving the file from the Hon'ble High Court my Ld Predecessor has called upon the petitioner to adduce additional evidence.

Thereafter, petitioner in addition to evidence of PW3, Ms Sunita Sukhija, Owner of Lazeez Affair, 6/48, Malcha Marg, Shopping Centre, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi has examined PW4 Krish Kumar, Assistant Manager, Lazeez Affairs as well as PW5 Ms Neha Gupta, Assistant Ahlmad in the Court of Ms Ankita Lal Ld MM02, Patiala House Court, New Delhi to corroborate the version of PW3 qua the employment and salary of deceased Rakesh S/O Sanjhi Smt Praveen Bains W/O Late Sh Rakesh ... vs Munna Rai on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118580395/
2 Ram.
4.
I have heard ld. counsel appearing on behalf of petitioners and Ld Counsel for respondents.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submission made by them and I also perused the record.
MACT No.1011/2018 Old No. 275/2012 Praveen Bains Vs Munna Rai &
ors Page No. 3 of 5 5.

PW 3 has deposed before this Tribunal that deceased was working in their restaurant and the record of his ( deceased ) employment and salary was destroyed in fire occurred on 04.04.2013, but at the time of passing of award dated 16.05.2014 by my Ld Predecessor there was no evidence with regard to the fact that record of Lazeez Affair was burnt in fire or not.

And after remand back of present claim petition the petitioners have examined PW 4 Krish Kumar, Assistant Manager M/S Lazeez Affairs, who has deposed that he has been authorized by Proprietor of M/S Lazeez Affairs,
Ms Sunita Sukhija (PW3) to depose before the Court.
PW 4 deposed that deceased Rakesh was working as Assistant Manager, and was taking salary of Rs.16,000/ p.m at the time of accident.

PW5 Neha Gupta, Asstt. Ahlmad has brought the judicial file of case FIR bearing No. 0051/13 dt 04.04.2013 Ex PW5/A wherein it find mentioned that a fire was broke out there in Restaurant Lazeez Affairs in the intervening night of 3/4.04.2013.
The verbal version of PW3 and PW4 can be acted safely and employment of deceased and regarding the record pertaining to employment of deceased Rakesh could have been burnt in the fire.
PW4 has deposed that deceased Rakesh was his Senior at the time of accident.
P.W 4 has also deposed that he is presently getting a salary of Rs.31,000/ p.m., then definitely at the time of accident PW4 could have drawn less salary than the deceased Rakesh.
PW4 is getting salary of Rs.31,000/ p.m, it means that deceased's salary could have increased due to passes of tenure in his service.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 6.

So this Tribunal in view of the observations in preceding paragraph has assessed the income of deceased for the computation of compensation as Rs.16,000/ p.m.
7.

As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given MACT No.1011/2018 Old No. 275/2012 Praveen Bains Vs Munna Rai & ors Page No. 4 of 5 @ 50%.

sentences.text: 8. There are three L.Rs of deceased ie his wife, son and mother, at the time of accident, so deceased spending 1/3rd of his income on his personal expenses.
Therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.16,000/ (16,000/ + 8,000 - 8,000/) per month.
9. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
The age of the deceased was 36 years old at the time of accident (17/05/1976 CBSE certificate Ex PW1/2 )
A multiplier of 15 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 28,80,000/ (16,000/ x 12 x 15).
So an amount of Rs. 28,80,000/ in lumpsum is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.
